# Code review — September 2, 2026

Historical review of application code at `89ec9f0`. Ten distinct issues were confirmed and subsequently corrected. The original source references and reproductions below describe the baseline defects; the resolution table records the implemented fixes. P1 identifies confidentiality issues. P2 identifies reliability, correctness, or performance issues.

Reproductions use the real application assembly, isolated SQLite databases, synthetic credentials, and simulated HTTP responses. No requests were sent to OpenAI. PATH, fonts, and personal application data were not modified. Portability checks construct Linux/macOS contexts through production code and exercise syntax in the PowerShell runner; they are not full operating-system integration tests.

The historical local reproduction project is `artifacts/review-2026-09-02/Review.csproj`; results are in `artifacts/review-2026-09-02/evidence.json`. These artifacts are ignored by Git and target the original baseline. A successful historical probe confirms a defect, not a fix. The tracked regression suite is the current verification source.

## Resolution and verification

The implementation followed the recorded plan: address credential handling first, extend operation deadlines, correct chat/risk/shell behavior, then correct pricing and indexed summaries. All ten findings have regression coverage.

| Finding | Implemented correction | Regression coverage in `PromptMeUp.Tests` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Redact quoted JSON assignments and decoded serialized JSON strings while preserving valid structure and safe adjacent text. | `PrivacyRegressionTests`, `AuthorizedCommandWorkflowTests.RunAsync_JsonCredentialsInStreams_RedactsProviderFollowUp` |
| 2 | Reject new credential-bearing preambles in setup and persistence; sanitize legacy settings before use; recheck provider-bound preambles. | `PrivacyRegressionTests.SaveSettingsAsync_CredentialPreamble_RejectsWithoutPersistence`, `LoadSettingsAsync_LegacyCredentialPreamble_SanitizesBeforeUse`, `OpenAiServiceRegressionTests.SendAsync_CredentialPreamble_RejectsBeforeProviderRequest` |
| 3 | Persist error types and stable metadata without raw exception messages or nested exceptions. | `OpenAiServiceRegressionTests.AssessAsync_ProviderEchoesCredential_PersistentLogExcludesExceptionDetails`, using the real Serilog pipeline |
| 4 | Share one deadline across HTTP sending and bounded body reading; record complete duration; preserve caller cancellation. | `OpenAiServiceRegressionTests` slow-body, successful-duration, caller-cancellation, and oversized-body tests |
| 5 | Include redirected streams in the command deadline, return captured prefixes on timeout, and propagate external cancellation. | `CommandExecutionServiceTests`, including an exited parent with a sleeping child holding inherited pipes |
| 6 | Recognize complete diagnostic forms, reject compound/evaluated shapes from low risk, and detect branch/file mutations. | `CommandRiskAssessmentTests` mutation and inspection theories |
| 7 | Render completed answers before memory maintenance; apply character limits to user input; prune oversized complete turns. | `AiConversationWorkflowTests.RunQueryAsync_LongAnswer_RendersAndCompletesSession`, `ConversationMemoryTests` |
| 8 | Request PowerShell 7 syntax with platform-appropriate paths on all supported operating systems. | `RuntimeContextServiceTests.Build_UnixPlatform_RequestsPowerShellSyntax` |
| 9 | Choose the documented model-specific band from actual input usage, including dated model snapshots; leave missing/unknown prices unavailable. | `ModelPricingPolicyTests`, provider-to-SQLite long-cost and unknown-model regression tests |
| 10 | Restrict aggregation to the current month before scanning rows. | `RequestSummaryRegressionTests`, checking both production SQL query plan and period totals |

Validation: preflight, restore, formatting verification, XML method comments, Release build with warnings as errors, and **148/148 tests** passed on Windows. This adds 58 cases to the 90-test baseline. Five isolated CLI smoke checks passed: help, version, Italian/Vietnamese status, and French attribution. No real provider request, credential, PATH change, or font change was used. `git diff --check` passed.

The inherited-pipe regression confirms bounded return after the root process exits. The runner does not provide OS process isolation or guarantee termination of a detached descendant whose parent has already exited. Legacy preamble cleanup updates the active settings row, not old backups or historical records. Unix context tests are deterministic snapshots; native Linux/macOS execution is validated by CI. Model-threshold sources and missing-price behavior are documented in [the cost guide](../../docs/OPENAI_COSTS_AND_CACHING.md).

## Original findings

1. **[P1] Credentials inside JSON text escape redaction.**

   Source: `PromptMeUp/Services/SensitiveDataRedactor.cs:36`; provider follow-up path: `PromptMeUp/Application/AuthorizedCommandWorkflow.cs:103`.

   The assignment regex requires the field name to be followed directly by whitespace and a colon or equals sign. Quoted JSON keys, such as `{"password":"<value>"}`, do not match. When JSON is embedded in stdout or a message string, `ActivityAuditService` also treats it as text rather than a nested object. A command that prints configuration can therefore cause a recognizable password to be persisted and sent in the next AI turn.

   Evidence `01-json-credentials`: both `SensitiveDataRedactor.Redact` and the SQLite `command_output` event retain the synthetic value. Recommended correction: recognize quoted keys and serialized JSON text while retaining structural traversal for actual JSON objects. Cover user text, stdout/stderr, and persistence separately.

2. **[P1] Custom preambles can persist API keys in plaintext settings.**

   Source: `PromptMeUp/Services/DatabaseService.cs:184`.

   `SaveSettingsAsync` runs prompt-injection protection but writes `SanitizedText` without credential detection. That protection normalizes Unicode and checks hostile instructions; it does not redact secrets. A key accidentally included in the preamble is accepted, stored in `app_settings.custom_instruction`, and included in subsequent request instructions.

   Evidence `02-preamble-storage`: saving succeeds, and a direct SQL read returns the complete synthetic key. Recommended correction: reject recognizable credentials before saving a preamble with a safe validation message, and define how to detect and clean existing affected settings without copying their contents into logs.

3. **[P1] Provider error messages reach diagnostic logs without redaction.**

   Source: `PromptMeUp/Services/CommandRiskAssessmentService.cs:68`; exception construction: `PromptMeUp/Services/OpenAiService.cs:287`. The orchestrator catch follows the same logging pattern.

   The provider's `error.message` becomes the message of `OpenAiRequestException`. The optional review catch passes the complete exception to the logger, and the sink configured in `Program.cs` includes `{Exception}`. If a provider error includes a credential or other sensitive content, that detail is written verbatim, even when the existing redactor could recognize it.

   Evidence `03-exception-logs`: a simulated HTTP 400 traverses the real OpenAI service and risk-review catch; the real Serilog file contains the synthetic key. Recommended correction: record the stable error code, HTTP status, and request ID; sanitize any retained diagnostic details and inner exceptions before persistence.

4. **[P2] The HTTP timeout does not cover response-body reading.**

   Source: `PromptMeUp/Services/OpenAiService.cs:281-284`.

   The request uses `ResponseHeadersRead`; the subsequent `ReadAsStringAsync` receives only the caller's cancellation token. HttpClient's timeout coverage ends when headers arrive. A stalled or slow response body can therefore keep the CLI waiting beyond the configured deadline. The stopwatch also stops before body reading, understating the duration shown and recorded.

   Evidence `04-http-body-timeout`: a 100 ms timeout and an 800 ms body delay still produce a successful response after 826 ms; the recorded duration is 7 ms. Recommended correction: use one explicit deadline across sending and reading, bound response size, and stop timing when the response is actually complete.

5. **[P2] Inherited child-process pipes can outlive the command timeout.**

   Source: `PromptMeUp/Services/CommandExecutionService.cs:60-64,82-83`.

   The timeout token is used to wait for the main process, while stdout/stderr readers use the external cancellation token. If the main process exits but a child keeps its streams open, the service remains blocked on the readers. Timer cancellation does not interrupt those waits, and the result can incorrectly report `TimedOut=false`.

   Evidence `05-process-pipe-timeout`: an inert child only sleeps for seven seconds; with a five-second timeout, the service returns after 8,181 ms with `TimedOut=false` and exit code zero. Recommended correction: include stream completion in the overall deadline and explicitly handle surviving descendants and open handles after the parent exits.

6. **[P2] The diagnostic allowlist assigns low risk to mutating commands.**

   Source: `PromptMeUp/Services/CommandRiskAssessmentService.cs:137`.

   The rule accepts the `git branch` prefix regardless of arguments and an initial `Get-*` without validating the rest of the pipeline. Earlier rules do not recognize `Set-Content`. Consequently, `git branch -D review-placeholder` and `Get-Date | Set-Content -LiteralPath review-placeholder.txt` are described as primarily diagnostic with a score of 15/100.

   Evidence `06-local-risk`: both scores are 15; the strings were assessed only and never executed. Explicit authorization remains enforced, but the risk guidance is misleading. Recommended correction: inspect command arguments, pipelines, and redirections; assign low risk only when the entire command is recognized as read-only.

7. **[P2] A completed AI answer can be discarded before the user sees it.**

   Source: `PromptMeUp/Application/AiConversationWorkflow.cs:385-387`; limit check: `PromptMeUp/Services/ConversationMemoryService.cs:45`.

   `MaxMessageCharacters` also applies to assistant messages. The workflow adds an answer to memory before displaying it; an oversized answer throws `ConversationLimitException` and nothing is rendered. The setting can legitimately be as low as 500 characters, while the response budget is in tokens and is not adapted to this limit. The user can lose an answer already generated and accounted for.

   Evidence `07-assistant-limit`: a four-character input, a valid 500-character limit, and a 501-character simulated answer yield one completed provider call, zero rendered answers, and an aborted query. Recommended correction: separate user-input and assistant-memory limits, and preserve answer visibility when its content must be excluded from or bounded in future context.

8. **[P2] Linux and macOS instructions recommend a different shell from the execution runner.**

   Source: `PromptMeUp/Services/RuntimeContextService.cs:97-98`; runner: `PromptMeUp/Services/CommandExecutionService.cs:106`.

   The authoritative context sent to the model recommends POSIX syntax, but the runner always starts `pwsh -NoProfile -NonInteractive -Command`. A POSIX environment assignment before a command, such as `VAR=review-placeholder echo harmless`, does not have that meaning in PowerShell. Commands valid for the advertised shell can fail or behave differently after approval.

   Evidence `08-shell-mismatch`: both Unix contexts select POSIX, the real `ProcessStartInfo` selects `pwsh`, and the harmless syntax probe produces stderr in the runner. Recommended correction: align runtime context and prompts with the actual shell; under the existing repository requirement, request PowerShell 7 syntax on Unix as well.

9. **[P2] Cost estimation always ignores long-context prices.**

   Source: `PromptMeUp/Services/DatabaseService.cs:360`; caller: `PromptMeUp/Services/OpenAiService.cs:298`.

   The parser and database retain both pricing bands, but `FindModelPriceAsync` always filters `context_window = 'short'`. `ResolvePriceAsync` does not receive the token count needed to choose a band. For requests subject to long-context pricing, the estimate and persisted cost history are incorrect.

   Evidence `09-long-context-pricing`: with 400,000 input tokens and synthetic rates of short=1 and long=2 USD/million, the service estimates USD 0.40 using short; calculation with long would be USD 0.80. These are fixture values, not current OpenAI prices. Recommended correction: choose the band using the model's applicable tariff threshold; show the estimate as unavailable when the necessary pricing data cannot be resolved.

10. **[P2] Daily and monthly summaries scan the entire request history.**

    Source: `PromptMeUp/Services/DatabaseService.cs:455-462`.

    Time filters exist only inside aggregate `CASE` expressions. Without a `WHERE` predicate on `occurred_unix`, the existing index does not restrict reads to the current month. The work required by `GetOverviewAsync`, used by status and cost screens, grows with all retained history even though the requested figures cover only today and this month.

    Evidence `10-summary-full-scan`: `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` on the SQL extracted directly from production source returns `SCAN ai_requests`. Adding the equivalent predicate `WHERE occurred_unix >= $month` changes it to `SEARCH ai_requests USING INDEX ix_ai_requests_occurred (occurred_unix>?)`. Recommended correction: restrict the time interval before aggregation and verify equivalent totals. No latency measurement was taken against the user's actual history.

Validation: all ten dedicated reproductions confirmed the defects. The full repository gate passed with zero build warnings/errors and 90/90 existing tests; isolated help/version CLI smoke tests passed. The existing suite does not cover the reproduced failure cases.
